experiment_lineage.hypothesis: Formation energy and on-hull probability depend on realized periodic local bonding: smoothly counted contacts near the sum of covalent radii encode coordination, bond-length strain, chemical ordering, and electronegativity contrast that global composition and minimum-distance features omit.

Nonlinear intensive measures of cell openness and lattice shape identify sparse, vacuum-dominated, or highly open structural regimes where linear raw volume-per-atom extrapolates poorly; these regimes should alter formation-energy prediction and may affect hull calibration.

Stability-related signals depend on how electronegativity and size contrast are distributed among realized local environments, not only their composition-wide or bond-wide averages. Balanced site fields and chemically disassortative contacts may capture network organization, while concentrated ionic load or strain-coupled contrast may mark heterogeneous environments.

The E03 site-resolved chemical-field signal is useful only when conditioned on structural regime. Adding robust openness and normalized-contact controls should prevent sparse-cell extrapolation while retaining local chemical-organization information.

Site-to-site distributions of first-shell coordination and normalized bond-length distortion encode packing topology that global minima and volume omit; if this is the main source of E04's gains, a chemistry-free topology set should retain substantial performance.
